identity.fantasy: An immortal night-beast tank that survives through avoidance, thick hide, infected wounds, marks, howls, and relentless life theft.
identity.one_line: A durable beast tank built on high avoidance, thick pelt, marks, howls, infections, and constant self-recovery. It turns being in the fight into healing and mitigation, and recent builds consistently label it a dungeon and raid tank.

mechanics.core_loop: Use Rotclaw as the stable attack, maintain Eternal Curse and the chosen mark, generate frequent weapon and bat procs through fast attacks, and layer Blood Howl, Blood Moon, infections, avoidance, and leech so incoming pressure continuously feeds recovery.
mechanics.single_target: Fast dual-wield attacks are currently recommended to drive leech, bat, and enchant procs while Rotclaw and marks maintain threat.
mechanics.aoe: Blood Plague, Festering Maw, howls, and infection effects spread threat and recovery, though the strongest recent weapon discussion focuses on single-target proc frequency.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Uncanny Movement and Speed, howls, and form mobility help connect pulls; personal survival states transfer more cleanly than target-specific marks.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Heightened Reflexes, Thick Pelt, Eternal Resolve, Bloodguard, Rejuvenating Shadows, and constant leech form a layered avoidance-and-recovery defense.
mechanics.group_utility: Howls, marks, and durable threat control support the group, but the specialization's primary contribution is staying alive without monopolizing healer attention.

failure_modes.text: Losing attack uptime cuts both damage and proc-driven healing, so avoidance alone cannot replace active contact.

Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: uncanny movement and speed, howls, and form mobility help connect pulls; personal survival states transfer more cleanly than target-specific marks.

Spending recovery or control too early leaves less protection for the next pressure event: heightened reflexes, thick pelt, eternal resolve, bloodguard, rejuvenating shadows, and constant leech form a layered avoidance-and-recovery defense.

append_claims.text: A July 30 Bloodmage leveling discussion recommends Eternal over Accursed for solo play, while another level-60 player characterizes its dungeon loop as heavily centered on Rotclaw and notes the permanent beast-form aesthetic.
append_claims.notes: Subjective descriptions from a small thread.

append_claims.text: An August tank-weapon discussion argues that Eternal should dual wield fast one-handed weapons because extra attacks and two agility proc enchants substantially increase leech, bat procs, and single-target self-healing compared with a two-hander.
append_claims.notes: Anecdotal target-dummy and dungeon experience, not controlled mitigation testing.

append_claims.text: The August Mythic inventory lists 120 Eternal records. The DPS compilation's 2,580 value is explicitly an Eternal DPS/off-role signal and is not a tank-performance measure.
append_claims.notes: Representation and off-role damage cannot establish mitigation strength.

append_claims.text: Eternal is an avoidance-and-leech tank whose survival engine depends on maintaining offensive contact rather than pausing behind purely passive mitigation.
Because many Eternal recovery effects are triggered or sustained through attacks, forced downtime reduces both threat and self-healing at once.
append_claims.notes: The sensitivity to downtime is not quantified.
